items.title: 53571_Mary Lou Williams oral history interview
items.q: He said, 'Why don't you go with her, Nelly?' ... Nelly, his wife was talking to him.

ctx.x: I hope. Mary, once you went through this period of praying and being away from music and in the church, what was the reaction of the people aside from Dizzy that you knew in the jazz world, to what was happening?

Not immediately. I used to give prayers for musicians and Monk, Hal Baker, Bud Powell in the summer would meet me at the Lady of Lourdes. Mass went on at 6:30 then, I think, or 7. They'd meet me at 6 o'clock and they'd go in church with me. I'd keep them through three masses. The first time I took Monk to church, it wasn't during mass, it was in the afternoon. I said, 'Come on and meditate.' He told his wife, why don't you go with Mary? She said, 'Oh, go ahead, Monk,' so he finally made up his mind. He said, 'Why…
